messages:
From: lauren.bishop@redwood.ai

Subject: Quick recap + initial model shortlist for PoC

Hi Sam / Priya —

Thanks again for taking the demo earlier. Per our conversation, I wanted to capture the key requirements and share an initial shortlist of models that we think map to ACME's goals for the proof of concept: high throughput for batch document processing, sub-300ms 95th-percentile for short classification calls, and strong hallucination/faithfulness on safety-critical extraction.

Key notes from the call
- Volume profile: ~200k docs/day initially, spiking to ~500k for monthly runs; average doc length ~600 tokens; some long tails up to 3k tokens.
- Latency SLO: interactive admin UI needs <300ms P95 for short queries; background batch jobs can tolerate higher latency with autoscaling.
- Quality constraint: extraction accuracy (entity + numeric fields) must be >= 92% on your labeled set.
- Security: ACME will prefer VPC/private deployment for production.

Initial model shortlist (recommendations rationale attached)
1) OpenTransformer-XL-13B (quant-4): best cost / throughput balance for bulk inference; good latency when sharded; slight drop on ultra-rare entities in our evals (~1.5% lower vs larger models).
2) Redwood-Safety-FT-7B: optimized for extraction with safety fine-tuning; excellent F1 on named-entity extraction at moderate cost but higher latency for long-context slices.
3) Titan-70B-INT8 (hosted): top-quality outputs and resilience to prompt drift; higher cost and requires dedicated capacity for consistent P95s.

I've attached a short spreadsheet with per-model cost/latency/quality rows plus the prompt set and benchmark summary PDF. Also shared the Drive folder with the eval notebooks and raw results.

Next steps (proposed)
- ACME to confirm primary success metric (accuracy vs latency tradeoff) by EOD Friday.
- Redwood to run a focused eval on a 1k-sample labeled subset (we can run two configs: throughput-optimized and quality-optimized). Estimated runtime: 48 hours.
- If ACME agrees, we’ll schedule a 30-min follow-up next week to review eval artifacts and adjust shortlist.

Would you prefer we prioritize the throughput (OpenTransformer path) or quality (Titan path) for the first 1k-sample run?

Thanks,
Lauren

Hi Lauren —

Appreciate the clear recap and the shortlist. A few quick clarifications from our side:
- Primary metric is extraction accuracy (we can tolerate up to 400ms P95 for the admin UI during the PoC).
- Security: we'll start with hosted but will move to Private (VPC) for prod; for the PoC we need an NDA + SOC2 attestation before we share the full labeled set.
- On cost: we’re budgeted for a mid-range option but want to see the delta on accuracy between 13B quant and the 70B INT8 before committing.

We agree to the 1k-sample focused eval. Please proceed with both configs (throughput-optimized and quality-optimized). Can you have the results ready for a review on Tuesday 2026-09-14?

Also loop in procurement if there are any contract addendums for Private deployment.

Thanks,
Sam

Date: 2026-09-08T16:48:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick recap + initial model shortlist for PoC

Thanks Sam —

We’ll start the two-panel eval tomorrow morning. A few operational notes:
- NDA & SOC2: Rachel, can you share the standard SOC2 attestation + short checklist back to Sam? I’ll attach the NDA template after legal quick review.
- Data ingestion: Diego will share the secure upload instructions (S3 presigned or SFTP) after we confirm the NDA.

Benchmarks & prompts we will run (links in Drive)
- Prompt set v1 (attached): includes extraction templates, guardrails, and edge-case prompts.
- Eval suite: accuracy on labeled fields, false-positive rate for entity insertion, token-level hallucination checks.
- Two configs:
  a) Throughput-optimized: OpenTransformer-XL-13B quant-4, batching, KV-cache enabled. Expected cost: low. Expected P95 for short queries: ~220-280ms.
  b) Quality-optimized: Titan-70B-INT8 hosted on dedicated capacity; lower batching, autotuned kernels, expected higher cost but P95 around ~180-240ms and best accuracy on rare entities.

Quick rationale (why not the 7B-only path first)
- Redwood-Safety-FT-7B performed well on extraction but regressed on numeric field normalization in our internal tests when prompts contained non-standard invoice formats. Given ACME's financial extraction requirements, we want some headroom. Starting with 13B vs 70B will reveal whether quantization + optimization is sufficient.

Deliverables we’ll provide to ACME after the run
- Eval notebook + raw metrics CSV
- Per-field confusion matrices and example failure cases
- Cost/latency projection sheet for scale to 500k/day

Proposed calendar
- 2026-09-09: start eval run (both configs)
- 2026-09-11: interim slack update with early signal (if any)
- 2026-09-14: 30-min demo of results + next-step recommendation

If that timeline looks good I’ll schedule the review.

—Lauren
